evidence.summary: Trailing-partial-group misassignment confirmed at K=48, group_size=32 (K%16==0, so no k-tail confound). Wrapper produced num_groups=1 and g_idx=0 for all 48 columns while the contract mapping is 0 for k<32 and 1 for k>=32; the second of the ceil(K/gs)=2 supplied scale/zero rows is never read. Kernel output is bit-close to the "clamped" model (max abs err 7.6e-6) and far from the contract reference (max abs err 25.65 on |C|max 26.82, rel 0.956, allclose False). Controls with K divisible by group_size (K=64/gs=32 and K=32/gs=32) match the contract reference to 9.5e-6 and 0.0, confirming the packing/zero+1 reference model is right and isolating the defect to the floor+clamp group derivation at lines 69-73.

rationale: Lines 69-73 use floor division for the group count and clamp, which is only equivalent to k // group_size when group_size divides K. The problem explicitly defines group_of(k) = the group column k belongs to for any K and states ceil(K/group_size) rows are supplied.

scope_evidence.summary: "every column must be dequantized with the scale and zero-point of the group it actually belongs to, for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size... scales and zeros are supplied with ceil(K / group_size) rows accordingly."
num_groups = K // group_size; g_idx = clamp(arange(K)//group_size, max=num_groups-1) — floor count plus clamp collapses the trailing partial group into the previous group.

scope_rationale: problem.txt states the contract must hold "for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size", and that scales/zeros are supplied with ceil(K/group_size) rows. K=40 with group_size=16 is a representative case the contract explicitly admits; the group table is derived inside the wrapper so the caller cannot compensate.
statement: For K not an exact multiple of group_size (e.g. M=64, N=64, K=40, group_size=16, bits=4), gptq_matmul's wrapper computes num_groups = K // group_size = 2 and clamps g_idx to num_groups-1 = 1, so the trailing columns k=32..39 are dequantized with row 1 of scales/zeros instead of their own final-group row 2; the last of the ceil(K/group_size)=3 supplied rows is never read and the output columns' contributions from k>=32 are wrong by the ratio of the two groups' scale/zero pairs (expect large, non-tolerance-level error, e.g. max abs error comparable to the magnitude of C itself, while a matching-K case with K=32 agrees).

data.expected_signal: K=16 < gs=32 gives num_groups=0 and g_idx=-1; kernel output should match a reference built from the SENTINEL row placed immediately below the scales/zeros base (proving a below-base read) rather than the supplied row 0.

evidence.summary: Negative-index below-base read confirmed at K=16 < group_size=32 (K is a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16, so the k-tail defect is not active). num_groups=0 makes g_idx == -1 for every column. I allocated scales/zeros with an extra SENTINEL row physically preceding the supplied tensor (supplied = view starting at physical row 1, scales stride0=64, zeros stride0=8) so the below-base read is directly identifiable. Kernel output matched the sentinel-row reference EXACTLY (max abs err 0.0) and was wildly off the contract reference (max abs err 515.84 vs |C|max 19.35; out |max| 514.23). Result was deterministic across two runs, i.e. a silent wrong-answer out-of-bounds read rather than a fault.

rationale: torch.clamp(..., max=-1) forces all entries to -1 when num_groups is 0; lines 43-44 add g_idx*stride to the base pointers with no bounds check, so negative indices produce below-base reads.

scope_evidence.summary: Contract holds "for any K"; scales/zeros supplied with ceil(K/group_size) rows, so K=8 with group_size=16 is a legal input with exactly one group row.
num_groups=0 gives g_idx=-1 everywhere; kernel adds g_idx*stride_scales / g_idx*stride_zeros to base pointers unguarded.

scope_rationale: problem.txt requires the mapping to be correct "for any K"; K smaller than group_size yields ceil(K/group_size)=1 valid group row, a case the stated contract admits. No test.py narrows the domain (test_code is empty, meta.json has passed=null), so the contract text is the only scope authority.
statement: When K < group_size (e.g. K=8, group_size=16, ceil = 1 group row supplied), num_groups = 0 so g_idx = clamp(..., max=-1) = -1 for every column; the kernel then loads scales/zeros at negative row offsets (scales_ptr - stride_scales), reading memory before the tensor base and producing wrong output (or an illegal-memory-access / nondeterministic result) rather than using the single supplied group row 0.

evidence.summary: Unmasked K-tail confirmed and isolated from the group-mapping defect. I used group_size=8 with K=40, so K is an exact multiple of group_size and the wrapper's g_idx equals the contract mapping (group_mapping_matches_contract=true) — any error is purely the unmasked third k-tile. Output was catastrophically wrong: max abs err 7.80e36 (ref |C|max 21.11, rel 3.7e35) at seed 2 and 1.97e25 (ref |C|max 23.11) at seed 3, i.e. garbage magnitude varying with heap contents rather than a bounded numeric drift. No NaN, deterministic within a run, no CUDA fault raised — a silent OOB read of A cols 40..47, packed-B row 5 and g_idx[40..47] accumulated into the result. Control K=32/gs=8 (K%16==0) matched the reference exactly (max abs err 0.0).

rationale: Lines 42, 47-48 have no offs_k + k*BLOCK_SIZE_K < K predicate and no other=0 on b/g loads, while the loop trip count is ceil-based.

scope_evidence.summary: "for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size" admits K values such as 40 that are also not multiples of the kernel's internal BLOCK_SIZE_K=16.
Loop over cdiv(K,16) tiles; a-load masks rows only, b-load and g_idx-load are unmasked, so the tail tile reads past the end of A, b_packed and g_idx and adds the result into the accumulator.

scope_rationale: The same "for any K" clause that makes non-multiple-of-group_size K legal also admits K values that are not multiples of 16 (e.g. K=40, which is a natural instantiation of the contract's trailing-partial-group case). Without a test.py the problem text is the operative input domain.
statement: For K not a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16 (e.g. K=40), the reduction loop runs num_pid_k = cdiv(K,16) = 3 iterations with no k-dimension mask: tl.load(a_ptrs, mask=a_mask) masks only rows, and tl.load(b_ptrs) / tl.load(g_ptrs) are fully unmasked, so the last iteration reads A columns 40..47, packed-B row 5 (beyond the K/8=5 rows) and g_idx entries 40..47 out of bounds and accumulates that garbage into the result — a wrong output (or OOB fault) independent of, and confounding with, the group-mapping defect.
